newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey seeks primary surplus of 4-5 percent of GNP.
newsitem.headline: Turkey seeks primary surplus of 4-5 percent of GNP.

text.p: Turkey aims to raise its primary budget surplus to 4-5 percent of gross national product over the medium-term from around two percent in 1996, a treasury official said.

"We must raise our primary surplus excluding interest towards 4-5 percent of national income," Treasury undersecretary Mehmet Kaytaz said in comments about a medium-term programme being prepared by the Treasury, central bank and state planning organisation.
Improving the primary budget result, which does not include interest payments on government debt, was linked to improvements in both revenue-raising and control of spending, Kaytaz said.
"What is important here is social security, privatisation, and the widening of the tax basis," he told Reuters.

Inefficiencies in tax collection and the sprawling social security system are at the heart of a budget deficit which reached 1,215 trillion lira in 1996. Privatisation officials have targetted sell-off revenues of $5 billion in 1997 as a key element of its balanced budget plans.
Economists have cast considerable doubt on the budget forecast.
"Until now the government has been relatively disciplined in its spending. But it is difficult to keep spending disciplined and low in a young country like Turkey," Kaytaz said.
